315: THE INSTITUTE
316-
317: IIFM was established as an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Agriculture in 1982 and later brought under the Ministry of Environment and Forest, Government of India. Since then, the Institute has developed itself as an educational, training, research and consultancy organization in the domain of environment and sustainability
318-
319- Vision and Mission
320-
321: The Institute, being sectoral in nature, imparts education in Forest Management, which is a judicious mix of Forestry, Environment, Social and Management sciences. It constantly endeavours to identify the problems of the community, especially the forest dwellers through need-based research and serves as a reservoir of knowledge in the area of forest management to catalyze integration of modern scientific and indigenous knowledge, suitable to the Indian context.  The Vision of the Institute, as identified in its Perspective Plan 2006-16, is:
322-
323: “To be among the leading international institutions in the area of environment, forest and development management and be respected, both nationally as well as internationally, for its outstanding contributions in the fields of education, training, research, consultancy and thought leadership.”
324-
325- The above vision is translated into the following Mission statements:
326-
    327-
  • 328: To serve different stakeholders of Environment, Forestry and Development sectors and the society in general, through the development of knowledge and its dissemination, human resource development through education and training activities and providing assistance in formulation and advocacy of relevant policies and strategies.
    • 329-
  • 330: To be a national institution with an international perspective and outreach.
    • 331-
  • 332- To build a culture of excellence, achievement, cooperation and service within a framework of strong ethical patterns of behaviour informed by universal values.

313: IIFM operates as a registered society under the governance of the IIFM Society and the Board of Governors. Academic decisions are entrusted to the Academic Council and the Faculty Council. The institute is structured into two primary divisions: The Academic Stream and the Administrative stream. Administrative stream supports academic initiatives under the supervision of Chief Administrative Officer and Director, who serves as the executive head of IIFM. Academic activities are coordinated by area chairpersons and task heads, with the versatile faculty playing a pivotal role in their execution under leadership of the Director IIFM. In essence, this organizational framework is designed to foster efficient decision-making and collaboration within IIFM, ensuring a well-coordinated approach to both educational delivery and administrative support.
